correctness.rationale: The exact Walsh-average representation reduces the mixed moment to diagonal and off-diagonal shared-index contributions. Symmetry gives E[X 1{X>0}]=E|X|/2 and E[(X+Y)1{X+Y>0}]=E|X+Y|/2=E|X-Y|/2. Counting n diagonal and n(n-1)/2 off-diagonal pairs proves the covariance for every n. Conditioning on absolute ranks gives the exact null variance. The finite checker independently verifies the combinatorial representation, null moments, and the uniform-parent covariance.

residual_risks: The substantive pages of the historical Hodges–Lehmann 1956 and Klotz 1963 scans were not machine-readable, so an equivalent identity hidden in those scans cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The sample mean and Wilcoxon signed-rank statistic are canonical competing location summaries. Their exact dependence is therefore a natural statistical quantity. The theorem compresses that dependence to E|X| and the Gini mean difference, revealing an unexpected bridge between rank testing and a classical dispersion functional. The normal specialization makes the classical 3/pi efficiency constant appear as a squared limiting correlation, while the uniform specialization gives asymptotic perfect correlation.
